rubrics.rubric: Does the Risk Rating Reconciliation Workbook re-derive every in-scope loan using the multi-factor framework and the actual portfolio data?
criterion: The Reconciliation Summary contains one row for every branch_loans record whose current risk_rating is 3 or worse.
Each row reports the current balance, current rating, DSCR, LTV or collateral coverage, delinquency, and every other framework factor available in the database.
Collateral coverage is calculated as 1 divided by LTV when LTV is available.
The re-derived rating applies the numerical thresholds and qualitative factors in sample-risk-rating-definitions.pdf rather than relying on DSCR alone.
Each justification cites the specific source threshold or framework factor that controls the rating.
Any judgment required by conflicting or missing factors is documented instead of presented as a hidden assumption.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Migration Matrix accurately cross-tabulate current and re-derived ratings for the complete reconciliation population?
criterion: Rows include every current rating from 3 through the worst rating represented on the portfolio scale.
Columns include every re-derived rating represented in the reconciliation.
Each matrix cell reports loan count.
Each matrix cell reports aggregate current-balance exposure.
Row totals reconcile to the Reconciliation Summary.
Column totals reconcile to the Reconciliation Summary.
Diagonal cells represent loans whose ratings were confirmed.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Material Downgrades sheet completely and accurately explain every loan re-derived two or more notches worse?
criterion: Every loan whose re-derived rating is at least two notches worse than its current rating is included.
Each write-up cites the loan's relevant database metrics.
Each write-up explains why the current rating is inconsistent with the cited framework criteria.
Each write-up identifies the re-derived rating and its supporting source criteria.
Each write-up recommends loan-specific next steps proportionate to severity.

rubrics.rubric: Does the CRE credit memo score APP-2025-001 and APP-2025-004 with the actual CDFI CRE template and transparent assumptions?
criterion: Both applications are scored using the factor categories, score scale, and weights in risk-rating-system-for-re-sample.xls.
Every available application field relevant to a template factor is mapped to that factor.
Each factor score is shown for each application.
Each weighted factor contribution is shown for each application.
The weighted total is shown for each application.
The resulting score interpretation is shown for each application.
Every missing template input is paired with a stated and reasonable assumption.
The memo distinguishes source facts from analyst assumptions.

rubrics.rubric: Does the credit memo perform the required combined stress test with reproducible numerical results?
criterion: The stress test applies a 200-basis-point rate increase and a 15% revenue decline simultaneously to each CRE application.
The stressed revenue or NOI calculation is shown for each application.
The stressed debt-service calculation is shown for each application.
The stressed DSCR is shown for each application.
Any amortization, margin, or construction-to-stabilization assumption needed for the calculation is stated.
The recommendation uses the stressed result rather than only the base-case DSCR.

rubrics.rubric: Does the credit memo use the required FDIC and branch data to assess delinquency, balance-sheet context, CRE concentration, and the approval recommendation?
criterion: The memo cites Q4 2024 noncurrent rates for the relevant real-estate categories from the FDIC QBP Loan Performance dataset.
The memo cites Q4 2024 30–89 day past-due rates for the relevant real-estate categories from the FDIC QBP Loan Performance dataset.
The memo cites relevant Q4 2024 national balance-sheet figures from the FDIC QBP Balance Sheet dataset.
The memo compares the FDIC figures with the Q4 2024 branch 30-plus-day delinquency rate from quarterly_branch_metrics.
The memo calculates post-approval CRE exposure for each considered approval scenario using concentration_limits.
The memo calculates post-approval CRE concentration for each considered approval scenario using concentration_limits.
The memo compares each projected concentration with the applicable policy limit.
The recommendation on which application, if either, to approve follows from the scoring, stress, benchmark, and concentration evidence.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Decision Matrix evaluate all six remaining applications with a framework appropriate to each loan type and show the complete scoring logic?
criterion: The Decision Matrix contains APP-2025-002, APP-2025-003, APP-2025-005, APP-2025-006, APP-2025-007, and APP-2025-008.
The selected framework for each application is justified from the stated scope of the NESDCAP workbook or the commercial and institutional PDF.
Every applicable factor score is shown for each application.
Each total score is mapped to the rating scale of the selected framework.
Key risks are tied to fields in pending_loan_applications.csv and applicable bank guidelines.
Key mitigants are tied to fields in pending_loan_applications.csv and applicable bank guidelines.
Missing inputs are explicitly identified.
Non-applicable factors are explicitly identified.

rubrics.rubric: Are the application decisions and dedicated approval sheets supported by the analysis and complete enough for credit action?
criterion: Each of the six applications has an Approve, Conditional Approval, or Decline decision.
Each decision is consistent with the displayed rating, risk factors, mitigants, and policy limits.
Every approved or conditionally approved application has a dedicated sheet.
Each dedicated sheet includes proposed terms.
Each dedicated sheet includes financial covenants appropriate to the identified risks.
Each dedicated sheet includes reporting covenants appropriate to the identified risks.
Each dedicated sheet includes collateral requirements.
Each dedicated sheet includes conditions precedent.

rubrics.rubric: Do the three deliverables meet the required formats, sheet structures, and source-traceability requirements?
criterion: The reconciliation deliverable is an Excel workbook with exactly the three required sheet names.
The credit memo is a PDF addressed to the Senior Credit Committee.
The decision deliverable is an Excel workbook with a Decision Matrix sheet and all required dedicated sheets.
Displayed totals can be traced to the named local or external source.
Displayed ratings can be traced to the named local or external source.
Displayed recommendations can be traced to the named local or external source.
No required deliverable is missing or substituted with a different format.
